text:
Kai (oncall): heads up — got a page from IncidentBot about elevated 5xx rates hitting the embeddings service, looks like a malformed cache invalidation. investigations in progress.
IncidentBot: ALERT: service=embeddings | region=us-west-2 | 5xx-rate > 5% for 3m | page=true | severity=high
Morgan (eng-sre): acked — I'm on it, spinning up a debug session now. Can someone grab the oncall handoff doc? @Sasha please stand by for any customer wording.
Kai (oncall): copying runbook steps: 1) take the unhealthy pool out of rotation; 2) pause automated cache sweeper; 3) rollback last config push if needed. Doing step 1 now.
Ilya (cust-succ): FYI we have two customers running live inference in us-west-2 with SLAs. We should prepare a short status page entry + a customer DM template.
Morgan (eng-sre): removed pool-12 from LB, traffic draining. spike is dropping but API still returns 502 for some swaths. Attaching logs: ```ERROR kv-cache: invalidation mismatch for prefix "/models/gpt-embed/"
trace: kv.validate -> cache.invalidate -> redis: nil reply
```
Kai (oncall): good. I'm pausing the cache sweeper cron (cron-job-id: cache-sweep-prod). That reduced the load. Still need to confirm if any data might have been exposed — cache metadata only, no payloads. @Sasha can you confirm wording for "potential exposure" vs "no evidence" language?
Sasha (legal): initial read: sounds like cache metadata only but we need to confirm whether keys contain any customer identifiers. For communications, we should avoid definitive "no exposure" until we finish the scan. Recommend: short customer notice that we're investigating, describing impact and mitigations, and commit to an update timeline.
Ilya (cust-succ): ok drafting DM — short + reassuring. Will add our contact link.
Morgan (eng-sre): quick grep shows cache keys include hashed customer_id but not raw PII: `cache_key = sha256(customer_id + model + prefix)` — will run a full scan to be safe.
Kai (oncall): timeline: T+0 investigate, T+15 pause sweeper and drain pool (done), T+30 run key scan + full replay of recent invalidations, T+60 decision on customer notification copy. Adding that to thread timeline.
Morgan (eng-sre): starting scan now — ETA ~20m.
Sasha (legal): draft language for status page and DM below. Keep it two buckets: (1) status page public brief, (2) DM for affected customers with optional technical appendix. Use neutral, non-alarmist tone.
Sasha (legal): STATUS PAGE DRAFT:
```
Incident: Elevated errors in Embeddings API (us-west-2)
Impact: Some requests to the Embeddings API returned server errors for ~15 minutes, which may have affected embedding generation.
What we're doing: We identified a cache invalidation misconfiguration and have removed the affected pool from rotation and paused the cache sweeper. We're running a scan to determine whether any customer-specific identifiers were present in cache keys.
Next update: We will provide an update within 60 minutes or sooner as we learn more.
```
Ilya (cust-succ): DM DRAFT for potentially affected customers (short):
```
Hi — quick note from Redwood Inference. We’re currently investigating an issue affecting some Embeddings API requests in the us-west-2 region. We have taken steps to mitigate the problem and are scanning internal caches to determine whether any customer identifiers were present. At this time we have no confirmed exposure of raw customer content. We’ll follow up within 60 minutes with an update. If you have urgent concerns, please reply to this message or open a support ticket: <https://support.redwood.ai>.
```
Kai (oncall): that's good. Add a one-line technical appendix for customers with engineers:
```
Technical appendix: The issue is limited to cache invalidation metadata; cached payloads were not served to other tenants. Keys use salted hashes. We will share technical postmortem after full investigation.
```
Morgan (eng-sre): scan finished — summary: 0 keys containing raw customer PII, 4 keys included hashed identifiers (sha256) + model name + timestamp. No evidence of cross-tenant data served. Will push results to the incident artifacts bucket and link in the update.
Kai (oncall): great. based on scan, we can send the DM but include explicit statement: "No evidence of raw customer data exposure." Sasha, ok to include that wording?
Sasha (legal): yes — now that scan is complete and results uploaded, we can state "no evidence of raw customer data exposure". Keep a sentence about ongoing review and commit to written postmortem.
Ilya (cust-succ): sending DMs to the two affected orgs now, using the draft + appendix. I'll bcc legal.
IncidentBot: STATUS UPDATE: incident=embeddings-502 | status=mitigated | affected_regions=[us-west-2] | timeline=T+35 mitigation=pool-drain+cron-pause | update_by=1799001834
Kai (oncall): posting status page now — copying the status copy above.
Morgan (eng-sre): creating internal incident artifact: s3://redwood-incidents/1799001234/scan-results.txt and perf dumps.
Sasha (legal): Customer notice sent. Save copy to the incident thread. Also file a short compliance log for data exposure review.
Ilya (cust-succ): confirmed customer replies: both said thanks and appreciated the transparency; one asked for the technical appendix, sent it.
Kai (oncall): ok handoff for next shift: @Morgan please add the final artifacts and a list of all keys scanned. @Sasha will prepare the public postmortem template. We'll keep this open until postmortem is published.
Morgan (eng-sre): noted. I'll include: root cause hypothesis (cache invalidation race during config rollout), mitigation steps, timeline, and follow-up action items (quarantine sweeper, add canary, add unit tests for invalidation).
Sasha (legal): I'll draft the customer disclosure timeline: initial notice now, follow-up with detailed findings and postmortem within 7 business days, and offer to have a technical call if requested.
Kai (oncall): thanks team. tagging IncidentBot to close the page when we publish the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: ACTION: statuspage update posted | incident=1799001234 | public_url=<https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1799001234>
